newsitem.title: UK: Pace Micro sees no reason for shr price fall.
newsitem.headline: Pace Micro sees no reason for shr price fall.

text.p: Pace Micro Technology Plc said on Tuesday it knew of no reason for the recent fall in its share price.
At 1042 GMT it was down three pence per share at 59-1/2.
Pace shares slipped earlier in the day to an all-time low of 52p, as dealers said negative press comment weighed on the shares. Trading was active with volume reaching more than three million shares.

Dealers attributed the decline to a delayed reaction to a report last Friday in the Investors Chronicle. The magazine advised holders of the shares to sell, warning Pace's profits were likely to be squeezed.
The magazine added that Pace was still looking for a replacement for chief executive David Hood, who has said he will stand down when a successor is found.
Hood became sole chief executive in February after the departure of Barry Rubery, then co-chief executive. Rubery left the company due to "irreconcilable differences of management style."
At the same time, the company also warned its second- half profits would be no better than the first half, due to continuing uncertainties over digital broadcasters' launch timetables.
However, the shares recovered from their earlier slide by late morning and dealers said they had started to see buying interest in the stock.
"I think the stock was looking to find a level for two-way business," said one dealer. "I think we may have found that level now."
